items.title: Shigeru Miyamoto (Nintendo) received Japan's prestigious Order of Culture and used the press confere...
items.content:
Shigeru Miyamoto (Nintendo) received Japan's prestigious Order of Culture and used the press conference to talk about generative AI, what 'creating' actually means when tools automate execution, and why Kyoto (not Silicon Valley) produced Nintendo's design philosophy.

https://t.co/OtveOcQUX0

The Order of Culture (文化勲章) is one of Japan's highest honors, previously given to film directors like Akira Kurosawa and writers like Yasunari Kawabata. Japan basically put games in the same category as film and literature.

He talks about generative AI in a way I have not seen from many working creators. He distinguishes between "creating" and "working." Creation is the hard part: composition, direction, deciding what should exist. Work is execution, and work is satisfying in a way that can fool you into thinking you have created something.

He says even before AI, tools have always automated technique, from typewriters to desktop publishing. What gets exposed when that happens is whether you had vision and intent, or whether you were just good at execution. AI is doing the same thing at a larger scale, and he finds this encouraging.

"The scary thing is becoming satisfied with the work and mistakenly thinking you created something."

People told him for decades that he should go outside of Japan and be in a "global hub". He stayed in Kyoto anyway. His work became more successful overseas than at home. The reason, he says, is that the person on the other side of the screen is human, regardless of geography. Deep local rootedness kept him anchored in concrete experience rather than trend-following.

items.content:
Yesterday I spent all day typing this into Claude Code:

"Do a full security audit of this website and server"

On every single VPS (and site) I have

I already had automatic unattended upgrades with auto reboot for security updates in Ubuntu (reboot only takes 4 minutes so I think it's fine every few weeks)

Also isolated each VPS on Tailscale with special security policies (generated by Claude Code! so it can not access any other VPS (in case it gets hacked) and not even access my MacBook or iPhone unless I talk to it first

Also lots of user permission stuff isolating stuff to www-data to avoid root access for web services

Not the most fun stuff but essential

I think in addition to @yongfook's "marketing week" we now have to add one week per month of "security week" because with the models getting better our pre-emptive defense has to get better too

Luckily for us I think the attack and defense capabilities of AI models seems to somewhat match? So as long as we keep typing "do a security audit" regularly into our clanker we can keep it safe

I hope 🫨

✅ It is blazing fast ⚡️ decoding 2x-4x+ faster than the latest open-weight models.

✅ If you’re building your own vision models, there are 24 pages worth of appendix details (!!) that showcase all of our experimental findings from training to evals!

items.content:
Finally learnt how to make 🍿 popcorn in a pan

I wanted to stop using those microwave popcorn bags

Microwave popcorn bags used to have a PFAS bag lining but that got banned in EU and US, but they're still not great. They use cheap palm oil (highly saturated fat) and synthetic butter flavoring (2,3-pentanedione a chemical twin of diacetyl that was used before and banned)

1) put a kinda tall pan, like a sauce pan, on medium to high heat (I use 12/14 on electric stove)
2) then make the pan very hot first like the sides have to feel hot too
3) then spray the pan inside with extra virgin olive oil (maybe you can use butter too? I will try next time)
4) then cover the pan with corn, it shouldn't stack, just level
5) keep pan open and wait until one corn pops
6) once it pops, put the lid fully on and start moving it back and forth kinda shaking, so the corns don't burn
7) then it takes about same as microwave popcorn, like 3-4mins, then once it stops popping every few seconds stop it
8) then add salt and put in a bowl

That gets you healthy popcorn with just olive oil and salt!

I'm not sure about adding salt before or after btw, I'll try, one problem adding it after is you sometimes breathe in the salt when eating cause it doesn't stick so well to the popcorn
